Russia and China's relations have recently deteriorated due to the Moscow Pact. Russia and China had prior had relatively good relations, and Russia would like to restore those relations. Russia has invited China to talks on how tensions could be eased.
[Diplomacy] Russia invites china to talks on lowering tensions over the Moscow pact

It is very good that we finally are going to have this talk. It is critical to both of us to do so. We will not mince words today. Today is a day of serious talk and discussion. And I hope that you're truly ready to have this conversation.

In the very beginning of the formation of the Moscow Pact, it was stated that "It will also work towards free trade and closer economic union." Although we have no problem with Free Trade within Moscow pact members, increasing economic unionism has the potential to hurt Chinese business interests in Central Asia. The Central Asian nations of Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan, as well as Mongolia, joined in the finalization of the pact. It seems a little curious that ALL asked nations in Asia agreed to this.

Regardless, the issue must now be broached between us about the Central Asian nations. China and Russia are somewhat at odds here, but there was a little something called the SCO. The Moscow Pact essentially pushes China out of the picture in Central Asia and supplants the authority of the SCO in this regard. The SREB, Silk Road Economic Belt, has been an important plan for China in its economic path. Our trade shot up with Central Asia over the last 15 years, and as such the area is an important one to us. And should the SREB goes forward, this will only become more the case. Of course, the Moscow Pact presents a barrier to this project - Russia has to sign off on it, and SREB is not Russia's dream. SREB would be an alternate trade route to the Block Train that Russia prides itself on.

Let's be honest here: Chinese economic growth and influence over Central Asia has been rubbing Russia the wrong way. The Moscow Pact's dominion in Central Asia and Mongolia is not a simple good-faith defensive alliance. It would, by all appearances, be a way to shut down increasing Chinese trade, influence, and investment with these nations and assert Russian dominance in the area. It damages the SREB plan, steering everything into the Block Train path instead.

So yes, relations between us have indeed deteriorated. Perhaps Russia acted in haste with its Moscow Pact and failed to consider our interests. If this is so, then it is a remarkable shame that Russia would simply forget the desires of its friend. However, the composition of the deal asserts Russian dominion over the area in all economic senses, and it would seem to be a rather blatant attack, and we in China can only hope that this is not the case. Our businessmen are frustrated and our people are worse off for it.

To alleviate China's concern on the Moscow pact going against Chinese interests Russia offers China an observer seat on the pact so that they may be involved in the talks but will have no obligation that any of the other members have in the pact.

This is amenable, however, we would like to see if the Central Asian states and Mongolia would like to join the APP. Obviously as these are both defensive networks, this aspect is not an issue. Free trade between these areas would also not be an issue. What would be an issue is economic unionism. The APP is not an economic union so much as a network of agreement towards trade, defense, and diplomatic solutions. As such, if states were interested in being members of the APP and Moscow Pact the issue of economic unionism in the Moscow Pact would have to be resolved.

There's also the big question on our mind, as well as South Korea's, India's, Pakistan's, and we'm sure the Central Asian states' minds - whatever happened to the SCO?

Surely Russia does not have any issue with the Central Asian states deciding if they would like to work with the APP's goals for peace and prosperity on the continent, does it?

Rather than the nations being part of two defense networks, Russia proposes that the Moscow pact forbade any sort of economic unionism within the pact, although free trade agreements, diplomatic cohesion, and other agreements of cooperation will still be allowed.

Also I suppose the SCO is still around but the Moscow pact is more unified and centralized. Further it includes a few nations not in the SCO : Serbia and Armenia
This, in addition with China's observer status, would be an amenable deal. Hopefully the tensions that have been built up over this Pact can relax.
China will be granted observer status and no economic Unionism will be allowed in the pact.
